summary: Sanders County, MT Forest Service lookout built 1930, staffed until 1973, restored 1996 as a Passport in Time project, and burned in 2006.

facts.design: Gable-roofed L-4 cab on a 10-foot tower
facts.status_note: Burned in 2006 per FireLookout.com and the Forest Lookouts site; no source describes what remains on the peak today

events.note: Built by the Forest Service on what was then the Cabinet National Forest; one of four ready-cut lookout houses installed that year
A 15-foot snowdrift on the trail meant the post could not yet be manned
Jay Jopling listed as known lookout personnel
Snow and rain brought the roof down over the winter; workers from the Trout Creek district reopened the lookout that spring, with a chartered government helicopter ferrying crews and tools
Register dates the abandonment to 1973, the year much of the Trout Creek Ranger District was transferred to the Cabinet Ranger District

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates the abandonment to 1973, the year of a district transfer, and does not state a cause. FireLookout.com and the Forest Lookouts page describe 1973 as the last staffed season. The dates agree.

notes_for_editor: Built 1930, staffing to 1973, and the 2006 burn each rest on two or three sources; the Forest Lookouts page is an amateur site that quotes old newspapers, so the newspaper items are cited to it as secondary. Height: the record says height_m 4.6, but FireLookout.com and the Forest Lookouts page both describe a 10-foot tower (about 3.0 m). Not corrected because the source does not state the structure height directly; the editor may want to check. Elevation: record 2000.1 m, FireLookout.com gives 6660 ft (about 2030 m). Not corrected; checkable against USGS. The FFLA list shows Tower Gone with NHLR US 177, MT 16. No access or current-site information was found, so access is left out.
